questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
1. Location: I love the Bay Area and the fact that the campus is just 40 minutes away from San Francisco. 
2. Academics: I had heard many good things about the professors at Berkeley.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty straight forward. Just read the emails and you will be guided through orientation easily.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: No assistance needed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer:
The orientation (Golden Bear Orientation, GBO) had both positive and negative aspects. 
Positive: You are put into a random group with other exchange and transfer students (transfer students are students that change university half way through their undergraduate studies), so you get to meet many new people. This is one of your best chances to make american friends. 
Negative: Many of the activities were boring and I skipped 2/4 days of the orientation, as did most other students.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found off-campus housing through facebook groups. Just search things like "berkeley housing" on facebook and you will find the groups.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
I spend about 1 month before finding accommodation, so I would the search in good time and I would definitely recommend finding accommodation before arrival. 
I paid about 7000kr pr month for a single room with 2 roommates 2 blocks from campus. 

You can also go with co-op, which is definitely the cheapest option - probably about 6000kr pr month including food. However, you most likely be in a double or triple room, and some of the co-ops can be somewhat gross. 

A third option is the I-house, which is about 12000kr pr. month for a double room, but that is including food like co-op.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I would recommend applying for co-ops as soon as you get at this link:
https://bsc.coop/
as there is a long waiting list. Then you can always decide later what you want.
Also look for housing close to campus - most of the activities are around campus.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You do it online through Calcentral.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There were advisors that could help you.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all except 1 class. Some are pretty difficult to get into because exchange students can only register some time after the actual students at Berkeley.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be prepared and ready at the deadline so you can get as many courses as possible.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I got the impression that professors were way better at teaching than at UCPH, however, I know other students got the opposite impression - so it probably depends on your field of study and the professors you have.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took high level undergraduate courses, which is from 100-199. I think every BA exchange student at UCPH should have an easy time following these courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More interactive - so better in my opinion.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
MCELLBI 149 - The Human Genome (3 units) 
INTEGBI 134L - Practical Genomics (4 units)
NUSCTX 110 - Toxicology - Last time this course was taught. (4 units)
MCELLBI 198 - DeCal Neuroscience 101 (2 units)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Can highly recommend Practical Genomics for students in Life Sciences. Professor Peter Sudmant is an awesome teacher. At least go read the description of the course. 
If you want something easy, take DeCal courses. They are taught by other undergraduate (bachelor) students and are ungraded. Note that you can first sign up for the courses a couple of weeks before the semester starts.

It is really easy to get recommendations from your professors if you want - literally just email them and ask. Many of them will give you recommendations even though you are not active in classes.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Sim cards is surprisingly expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
It's pretty expensive to eat out at restaurants. You should give about 18% in tip if you are eating at a restaurant (but 0% if you are ordering take away). 
You also have to tip in a lot of other instances (e.g. at bars), so look it up so you don't tip too much.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't join a club, but I think it could have been fun.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I mostly went to frat parties, college football and basketball games. You can buy a season pass to all home football and basketball games for 125$.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I especially recommend going to the Berkeley vs Stanford football game.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Yosemite
Roadtrip on highway 1 to LA (although the city of LA sucks, the drive on highway 1 is amazing)
Go see redwood forrests
Enjoy SF, it's an amazing city - although there are many homeless people smoking crack downtown.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Live with Americans roommates by renting a room or live in a co-op (not many americans in the International house, obviously).
Talk to as many during the orientation (GBO mentioned above). The transfer students are americans that are transferring to Berkeley and thus they also don't know anyone. 
Just talk to random people - americans are very friendly and forward.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: called my professors by their first name in the start.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The very forward american attitude makes it easy to talk to people. Also the students of Berkeley are very diverse, so you learn a lot about other cultures.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Make the most of your academic experience. Go to office hours and talk to the professors. 
2. Go on trips. Even if you have a lot to do, you can go on day trips to SF or go hiking just north of Golden Gate. 
3. Look for accommodation and stipends early.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Be good at applying for stipends. I got all my cost covered.
You can get a good overview of some possible stipends at:
https://www.legatbogen.dk/

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being apart of another culture.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: There was a lot to think about in the start: Socialising, academics, practical information, housing, etc.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: There are some staff from Copenhagen that you can ask questions about the exchange stay, but they are pretty useless and can't answer many questions. So be ready to do some research of how to get visa, housing etc.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
